host:
Welcome to The Long and Short of It.
Today's contract: will the 10-year yield print at or above 5.00% on any observation through October 23rd?

Affirmative will make the case for yes.
Negative will make the case for no.
yes:
Affirmative.

The long of it is that this time is the same duration squeeze — only the who has changed. Overnight Reverse Repo (ON RRP) is a Fed facility, not a Treasury button, and take-up that peaked near two and a half trillion at the end of 2022 is now mostly under a billion day-to-day; the slogan that Yellen emptied it is the live narrative on trial, but the print is the drained buffer either way. Fear is that Secretary Bessent still has not delivered the duration extension he floated as the eventual goal — February 2025 he called terming out a long way off, and the August 2026 refunding kept coupon sizes flat for at least the next several quarters while leaning on bills as the shock absorber. Soft-landing hopes lean on Chair Warsh to cut; Trump said at nomination that Warsh certainly wants to cut rates, but Warsh's own Jackson Hole line in August 2026 put prices first with inflation still above target and work to do. Concession: August's ten-year auction still cleared with thin primary-dealer take-down and heavy indirect demand, so if Bessent's maintain-coupon path keeps clearing that way through the next refunding prints, the same machine can miss 5.00% by October 23rd. The captive-duration story on this site says actors who leave the cushion empty and coupons unextended still put the 10-year yield through the bar.
no:
Negative.

The short of it is that this time is different at who owns the plumbing and what they have actually done. Overnight Reverse Repo (ON RRP) rundowns when money-market funds stop submitting to the Desk — Fed mechanics, not a Yellen empty-button; treat that slogan as unverified. Hope is Bessent's path dependence: he criticized a bill-heavy mix before office, then as Secretary said terming out was eventual but not signaled now, and August 2026 refunding plus TBAC kept coupons flat with dealers generally eyeing size hikes sometime in 2027 — buybacks raised for long-end liquidity are not a coupon-duration extension. Soft-landing versus fiscal-dominance is on trial in the Warsh file: his record is inflation-accountability and a puzzled reaction to the September 2024 cut, while Trump's "certainly wants to cut rates" was Trump's claim about him, not Warsh's pledge — Jackson Hole was discipline, not a cut date. Concession: ON RRP near empty removes a cash sponge that existed into the October 2023 near-miss, when the 10-year yield peaked at 4.98% and never printed 5.00%, so a weak coupon-clearing print before October 23rd would put the same-machine story back up. Until Bessent actually raises coupons or Warsh delivers an easy path, the who-and-direction file argues the 10-yr yield stays under 5.00% through October 23rd.
close: This has been The Long and Short of It. Choose evidence over tribe.
